title: Presentable objects as small modules under a Gabriel--Popescu localization
statement:
Fix a universe $U$ for sets and Hom sets [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\mathcal C$ be a Grothendieck abelian category relative to $U$ [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. There exist a unital ring $R$ with underlying set in $U$ and additive functors $F:\operatorname{Mod}_R\rightleftarrows\mathcal C:G$ such that $F$ is left adjoint to $G$, $G$ is fully faithful, $F$ preserves finite limits and all $U$-small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and the adjunction counit $FG\to\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C}$ is an isomorphism. Here $\operatorname{Mod}_R$ is the category of left $R$-modules with underlying sets in $U$, with linear maps. These same $R,F,G$ have the following property for every uncountable regular cardinal $\rho\in U$ with $|R|<\rho$ and every $c\in\mathcal C$:
$$c\text{ is }\rho\text{-presentable}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists M\in\operatorname{Mod}_R,\ |M|<\rho\text{ and }c\cong F(M).$$
A cardinal $\rho$ is regular when a union of fewer than $\rho$ sets each of size less than $\rho$ has size less than $\rho$; a small category is $\rho$-filtered when every diagram with fewer than $\rho$ morphisms admits a cocone; $c$ is $\rho$-presentable when $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(c,-)$ preserves all $U$-small $\rho$-filtered colimits.

source.place: Remark A.4 and Lemma A.5, both implications (using only uncountable regular cardinals larger than the ring); Hall--Neeman--Rydh, Appendix A. Online source read; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this cardinal characterization.

proof.text: Choose a generator $P$ from the Grothendieck hypothesis. Apply the separator tensor--Hom lemma to obtain $R=\operatorname{End}(P)^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $F\dashv G$. The ring lies in $U$ because the Hom sets do. The cited lemma gives additivity, full faithfulness, finite-limit preservation and the invertible counit $\epsilon$. The left-adjoint colimit lemma gives preservation of every $U$-small colimit by $F$. In particular $F$ preserves kernels and cokernels, hence is exact. Fix these $R,F,G$ once, before choosing $\rho$.

source.place: Remark A.4: Gabriel--Popescu and the fixed adjunction

proof.text: Fix an allowed $\rho$ and a $U$-small $\rho$-filtered diagram $(x_i)$ with colimit $x$. Form $A=\varinjlim_iGx_i$ and its comparison $t:A\to Gx$, so $t a_i=G\iota_i$. This is a small module colimit: explicitly one can take the quotient of $\bigoplus_iGx_i$ by the relations identifying each element with its image under a diagram arrow. Compatible linear maps out of this quotient are exactly cocones. By preservation of colimits and naturality of $\epsilon$, $FA$ identifies with $x$, and $F(t)$ identifies with $\epsilon_x^{-1}$, hence is invertible. Exactness gives $F(\ker t)=F(\operatorname{coker}t)=0$. Also, if a submodule is generated by a set $S$ of size $<\rho$, its elements are finite sums of $rs$, encoded by finite lists in $R\amalg S$; the finite-list bound makes its cardinality at most $\max(\aleph_0,|R|,|S|)<\rho$.

source.place: Lemma A.5, forward implication: the comparison map and the bounded generated submodule estimate

proof.text: Let $|N|<\rho$ and $\phi:FN\to x$. Its adjoint is $n:N\to Gx$. Form $Q=N\times_{Gx}A$, with projections $p:Q\to N$ and $q:Q\to A$. Applying $F$ gives a pullback of the isomorphism $F(t)$, so $F(p)$ is invertible. Put $N'=\operatorname{im}p\subseteq N$. Choose a lift in $Q$ of every element of $N'$, and let $M\subseteq Q$ be generated by these lifts. Step 2 gives $|M|<\rho$. For $v=p|_M:M\to N$ we have $\operatorname{im}v=N'$, $\ker v\subseteq\ker p\cong\ker t$, and $\operatorname{coker}v=\operatorname{coker}p$. The latter is killed by $F$ because $F(p)$ is invertible; the kernel is killed by $F$ because it embeds into $\ker t$ and $F$ preserves monomorphisms. Thus $F(v)$ is invertible. The bounded-module presentability lemma factors $q|_M$ as $M\xrightarrow{b}Gx_i\xrightarrow{a_i}A$. Since $nv=ta_ib=G\iota_i b$, adjunction gives $\phi F(v)=\iota_i\epsilon_{x_i}F(b)$. Composing with $F(v)^{-1}$ factors $\phi$ through $x_i$. This proves surjectivity of the Hom-colimit comparison.

source.place: Lemma A.5, forward implication: pullback, bounded replacement and factorization; the two projections are written explicitly

proof.text: To prove injectivity, first take $h:FN\to x_i$ with $\iota_i h=0$, and write $n:N\to Gx_i$ for its adjoint. Put $z=a_i n:N\to A$ and $K=\ker z\subseteq N$. Under the identifications of step 2, $F(z)=\iota_i h=0$. Since $F$ preserves kernels, $F(K\hookrightarrow N)$ is invertible. As $|K|<\rho$, the bounded-module lemma applied to the two maps $K\to Gx_i$ given by $n|_K$ and zero gives an arrow $u:i\to j$ with $G(x(u))n|_K=0$, because their composites into $A$ agree. Adjunction now gives $x(u)h\,F(K\hookrightarrow N)=0$, whence $x(u)h=0$. For any two maps $FN\to x_i$ equal in $x$, apply this to their difference. For maps from different stages first move to a common stage by filteredness. This is exactly eventual equality in the set colimit of the Hom sets, so the comparison is injective. Together with step 3 it proves that $FN$ is $\rho$-presentable; an isomorphic object has the same property by precomposition with the isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma A.5, forward implication: explicit eventual-equality argument completing the Hom-preservation assertion

proof.text: Conversely let $c$ be $\rho$-presentable. The submodules $N\subseteq Gc$ with $|N|<\rho$ form a $U$-small poset: they are a subset of the power set of the underlying $U$-set $Gc$. It is nonempty and $\rho$-filtered. Indeed the sum of fewer than $\rho$ members is generated by their union, whose size is $<\rho$ by regularity; step 2 makes that sum small. Every element of $Gc$ lies in a small cyclic submodule by the same estimate. Thus the union is $Gc$, and this is its module colimit: compatible linear maps on the submodules glue uniquely on elements. Applying $F$ and $\epsilon_c$ exhibits $c$ as the colimit of the monomorphisms $FN\hookrightarrow c$; they are monic since $F$ preserves finite limits. Presentability of $c$ factors $\operatorname{id}_c$ through one such $FN\hookrightarrow c$. That monomorphism has a right inverse and hence is an isomorphism: if $ir=1$, cancellation of the monomorphism $i$ in $iri=i$ gives $ri=1$. Therefore $c\cong FN$ with $|N|<\rho$, as required.

source.place: Lemma A.5, converse: filtered union of bounded submodules and the split monomorphism
